summary: Adds app-owned user preferences: downstream projects persist their own per-user state under a reserved 'app' namespace in Profile.preferences (opaque to Dlux, cross-device), bounded by a size cap and served by a targeted concurrent-safe patch endpoint plus browser helpers. Adds a complete self-service forgot-password flow rendered in the Dlux login layout (all login styles, RTL/LTR, Arabic/English/custom languages), delivered through Dlux's own email transport and gated by a new 'forgot_password_enabled' setting that self-hides until email delivery is ready; the login page also shows a live lockout countdown instead of a generic error and a modern inline credential-error message. Plus a superuser 'Reset data' admin command that lists discovered models with row counts and clears selected ones (scoped models soft-deleted/recoverable, others permanent, optional media deletion) with System Settings, updater state, permission groups, and superusers always protected; a confirm-password prompt auto-hide fix; and the missing Arabic/English names for Dlux operational models. Inline-safe: no migration, JSON/view/static/template updates only.
highlights: App-owned user preferences: downstream projects persist their own per-user state under a reserved 'app' namespace in Profile.preferences (opaque to Dlux), with a size cap and a targeted, concurrent-safe patch endpoint plus window.getAppPreference/updateAppPreference helpers.

New self-service forgot-password reset flow in the Dlux login layout (multiple login styles, RTL/LTR, i18n), sent via Dlux email; gated by 'forgot_password_enabled' and auto-hidden until email is configured.
Login page shows a live lockout countdown (mm:ss) with a disabled submit button instead of a generic 'too many attempts' error.

New superuser 'Reset data' command: clear selected models' rows (scoped models soft-deleted/recoverable, others permanent) after current-password confirmation; System Settings, updater state, permission groups, and superusers always protected.
Fixed the confirm-password prompt so its warning no longer auto-hides, and translated the previously-untranslated Dlux operational model names.
